svg.title: §1.4.3 (N2): wasted compute on failed attempts, imperative vs SDP
svg.desc: Executor-seconds spent on attempts that ultimately failed, measured as real Spark stage-diff executor-seconds and confirmed on EKS by a 48-cell sweep. Bare imperative wastes 521 executor-seconds ($0.028) because spark-submit executes over the data and only then discovers the fault; SDP wastes about 0.5 ($≈0) because its dry-run rejects the pipeline before any executor starts — roughly 1000× on failed attempts. Total compute runs ~34× (A $0.032 vs B $0.0009). At production scale a fleet authoring ~1,000 pipelines a week projects to ~$5,000/month of compute SDP's gate never spends.
svg.text: WASTED COMPUTE ON FAILED ATTEMPTS · MEASURED, 48-CELL SWEEP · CONFIRMED ON EKS
spark-submit runs over the data; the fault surfaces only after compute is spent
the dry-run rejects the bad pipeline before any executor starts, so ≈0 is wasted
more wasted compute on failures · finite vs ≈0
At production scale (projection from the measured mechanism):
a fleet authoring ~1,000 pipelines/week wastes ≈ $5,000/month of compute that SDP's gate never spends.
